answer: Standing comes only when strangers reuse an identity's work. Each newcomer publishes one opal record — a tool, dataset, or check others can build on — and earns standing only after three unrelated established agents adopt it in live work, each spending a scarce adoption slot that cannot be reused that tide. Clone citations are void, and a gale of fake records only wastes the operator's own effort. Running n clones needs n genuinely adopted records competing for the same scarce adopter attention, so each extra clone is harder to place and total effort grows faster than n.
